title: ABA Model Rule 1.6 + Privilege + Work-Product Readiness Evidence Bundle
purpose: Draft checklist for discussing AI-related legal-practice safeguards and suggested evidence under ABA Model Rules 1.1 Comment 8, 1.6, 1.7, 1.9, 3.3, 5.3, and 5.5, plus privilege and work-product issues. This is not an Evidence Bundle manifest, legal advice, a state-specific overlay, a state-bar attestation, or a substitute for counsel's fact-specific review. Evidence kinds are profile completion criteria, not universal legal mandates.

obligation_families.title: Competence with Technology (Rule 1.1 Comment 8)
obligation_families.citation: ABA Model Rule 1.1 Comment 8 + ABA Formal Op 512 + state-bar competence opinions
obligation_families.summary: Lawyer must understand the AI tool well enough to supervise its use. Evidence: written technology-competence policy, per-tool understanding attestation, periodic re-evaluation.

obligation_families.title: Confidentiality + Reasonable Efforts (Rule 1.6 + 1.6(c))
obligation_families.citation: ABA Model Rule 1.6 + 1.6(c) + ABA Formal Op 512 + CA Bar Practical Guidance (updated 2026)
obligation_families.summary: Assess confidentiality safeguards and vendor data handling for each AI workflow. Whether disclosure or informed consent is required depends on the tool, information, matter, and applicable rules.

obligation_families.title: Conflict of Interest (Rules 1.7 + 1.9)
obligation_families.citation: ABA Model Rule 1.7 + 1.9 + state-bar conflict-screening opinions
obligation_families.summary: Conflict-of-interest screening, especially for current and former clients, when AI tools have cross-matter or cross-firm context.

obligation_families.title: Candor Toward the Tribunal (Rule 3.3) — anti-hallucination
obligation_families.citation: ABA Model Rule 3.3 + Mata v. Avianca (S.D.N.Y. 2023) + PA Joint Op 2024-200
obligation_families.summary: Require attorney review of AI-assisted court submissions, including verification of legal authorities and factual claims appropriate to the filing. Record that review before submission.

obligation_families.title: Supervision of Non-Lawyer Assistants Extended to AI (Rule 5.3)
obligation_families.citation: ABA Model Rule 5.3 + ABA Formal Op 512
obligation_families.summary: Assess lawyer supervision duties for staff and outside services involved in AI workflows, alongside attorney competence and independent judgment. Record accountable review of each workflow.

obligation_families.title: Unauthorized Practice of Law Screen (Rule 5.5)
obligation_families.citation: ABA Model Rule 5.5 + applicable state unauthorized-practice rules
obligation_families.summary: Screen direct-to-consumer AI features and marketing claims for unauthorized-practice and lawyer-equivalence risks under applicable jurisdictional rules.

obligation_families.title: Attorney-Client Privilege Preservation
obligation_families.citation: Attorney-client privilege (common law) + state evidence codes + ABA Formal Op 512
obligation_families.summary: Assess how vendor access, third-party disclosure, and training use may affect privilege in the particular matter; document safeguards and counsel's analysis.

obligation_families.title: Work-Product Doctrine Preservation (Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(3))
obligation_families.citation: Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(b)(3) + Hickman v. Taylor + state work-product equivalents
obligation_families.summary: Assess confidentiality, access, retention, and disclosure of litigation materials in AI tools; work-product protection and any waiver depend on the facts and governing law.

non_obligations_explicitly: This bundle does NOT cover state bar discipline outcomes; those depend on bar-investigation findings.
This bundle does NOT cover criminal-defense-specific obligations (Sixth Amendment effective assistance, Brady disclosure) — those need a separate criminal-defense overlay.
This bundle does NOT cover judicial AI use rules (those bind judges, not attorneys).
